title: General Internship Application 2027
description:
We are excited to announce an open call for talented interns to join Oklo's dynamic team! Below are multiple positions across various disciplines that may be available, offering the chance to work on innovative projects for Summer 2027. If you're passionate about solving complex challenges, thrive in a collaborative environment, and are eager to contribute to groundbreaking solutions, we encourage you to apply.
Requirements
Oklo interns are required to:
Relocate or be available to work out of Santa Clara CA where Oklo Headquarters is located for the duration of the internship or out of one of our satellite locations in Denver, CO, Brooklyn, NY, Idaho Falls, ID, or Washington D.C.
Be available to work 30-40 hours per week between June 7, 2027 - August 20, 2027 (depending on the scope of work)
Be currently enrolled or recently (2027) graduated with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree from an accredited university
Intern Position Descriptions
Core Thermal Hydraulics Intern
The CTH Intern will develop intermediate fidelity (IF) subchannel and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for applications in sodium fast reactors (SFRs). The project will involve comparisons between simulation results and experimental data. The exact topic will depend on interest and company needs but could cover fluid-structure interaction, turbulence model development, uncertainty quantification, or surrogate modeling.
Required Qualifications
Coursework in fluid mechanics and heat transfer
Experience with 3-D CFD and meshing workflows
Proficiency in Python
Clear technical communication and documentation skills
Bonus Qualifications
Experience with advanced 3-D CFD concepts (large eddy simulation, fluid-structure interaction)
Familiarity with high-performance computing workflows and tools
Experience with MOOSE
Familiarity with statistics and reduced order modeling
Materials Intern
Working with members of Oklo’s Materials Team, will help with the selection and qualification of materials for use in nuclear reactor systems. Typical work duties include computational model development and implementation, engineering analysis, documentation, and interfacing with our fuel fabrication and engineering teams.
Key Responsibilities
Analyzing material performance across expected operating conditions
Developing new analysis methods to predict material behavior in service
Performing engineering analyses, including assessments of thermal performance, mechanical performance, safety performance, manufacturability, and cost.
Collaborating cross-functionally to provide technical feedback to quick-iterating computational teams.
Authoring technical reports using modern documentation tools and techniques
Required Qualifications
Experience working with and developing material behavior models
Experience with material characterization (material testing, metallography)
Background in nuclear, chemical, materials engineering, or equivalent
Motivated learner who is adept at efficiently summarizing literature
Bonus Qualifications
Experience with engineering simulation software, such as ANSYS or COMSOL
Coding or data analysis experience (e.g., Python or similar tools)
Mechanical Analyst Intern
This intern will contribute to the evaluation and optimization of mechanical components that are critical to Oklo’s advanced power plant designs. This position offers hands-on experience in applying engineering fundamentals, performing structural analysis, and integrating results into design iterations.
Key Responsibilities
Apply first-principles mechanics and strength of materials to support analysis of structural components
Assist in summarizing mechanical analysis results for design teams, highlighting key findings such as peak stresses, margins of safety, and potential design revisions
Support the development of technical documentation, ensuring clear and concise communication of assumptions, methods, and results
Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and testing teams to help inform design improvements
Required Qualifications
Working toward a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline
Strong foundation in mechanics of materials, dynamics, and heat transfer
Exposure to FEA tools (e.g., Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL, or similar) through coursework or projects
Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or another programming language for basic data analysis or workflow automation
Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly document and present technical findings
Bonus Qualifications
Prior research or project experience involving creep, fatigue, or thermal-mechanical problems
Familiarity with engineering codes and standards (e.g., ASME, AISC, or similar)
Experience using Git or another version control system
Instrumentation and Controls Intern
This intern will contribute to the development, integration, and testing of measurement and control systems that support advanced reactor operation and power generation. This position provides hands-on exposure to sensors, automation, and control strategies, while giving interns the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges.
Key Responsibilities
Assist in developing and testing sensors, instrumentation, and actuators under real design constraints
Help design and implement control algorithms for equipment and processes
Support the integration of I&C components into reactor systems and analysis workflows
Contribute to documenting methods, results, and system designs in a clear and professional manner
Collaborate with design and analysis teams to provide feedback that supports rapid iteration and improvement
Required Qualifications
Working toward a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
Familiarity with measurement techniques, data acquisition, and signal processing
Exposure to control theory and feedback systems through coursework or projects
Basic programming skill

title: Propulsion Component Engineering Intern - Spring/Summer 2027
description:
Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage.


About The Role: 
As a Propulsion Component Engineering Intern, you will support the development of flight-critical mechanical and fluid system components, including valves, actuators, and integrated propulsion hardware. You will contribute to hardware development from clean-sheet design through build, test, qualification, and production, working closely with propulsion and vehicle teams. Your work will directly support systems operating in high-pressure, high-temperature, and dynamic flight environments.
 
Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April)
Responsibilities:
Support the development of propulsion components (e.g., valves, actuation systems, and fluid control hardware) from concept through flight-ready delivery
Contribute to designs for extreme environments, including high pressure, temperature, and transient operating conditions
Support engineering trade studies across performance, manufacturability, reliability, and testability
Assist with clean-sheet design, analysis, and integration of propulsion components
Support hardware through rapid build–test–iterate cycles
Participate in troubleshooting and root cause analysis during development and test
Work with propulsion and vehicle system owners to define requirements, interfaces, and integration strategies
Assist with system-level sizing, architecture, and design trades
Support development testing, qualification, and acceptance of flight hardware
Contribute to the transition from prototype to repeatable, production-ready designs
Assist in defining operational limits and evaluating reliability and safety across all phases of use
Apply engineering judgment and first principles to support risk-informed design decisions
Prioritize work effectively in a fast-paced, evolving development environment
Requirements:
Practical experience designing, building, and testing hardware or vehicles through internships, coursework, research, or hands-on projects
Must be currently enrolled in a STEM program at an accredited college or university (undergraduate student in your third or fourth year of study, or enrolled in a Master's or Ph.D. program)
Strong interest in propulsion systems, mechanical systems, and hardware development
Strong understanding of engineering first principles, including fluids, thermodynamics, mechanics, and materials
Demonstrated ability to work within cross-functional teams
Enthusiasm for aviation and Hermeus's mission
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
GPA of 3.0 or above
Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
Experience with propulsion systems, high-pressure fluid systems, or aerospace mechanisms through internships, coursework, research, or projects
Experience designing or building components such as valves, actuators, or fluid control hardware
Familiarity with high-temperature materials, sealing strategies, and common mechanical failure modes
Familiarity with GD&T, tolerance stack-up, and precision assemblies
Hands-on experience supporting hardware testing, assembly, integration, or troubleshooting
Experience with CAD tools (NX preferred) and analysis tools (ANSYS or similar)
Experience participating in rapid hardware development environments, including engineering competition teams, research programs, or internships
Scripting experience (Python, MATLAB, or similar) for analysis or automation
Additional Requirements:
Willingness to work hands-on in build, integration, and test environments
Ability to support extended hours during critical test campaigns
Willingness to travel to support hardware builds and flight tests
Must be eligible to access export-controlled information
The hourly rate listed for this internship is intended as a general guideline. Final compensation will be determined based on degree level.
Benefits:
Time Off: Interns are eligible for 5 days of sick leave and unpaid time off.
Office Perks: Weekly paid office lunches and fully stocked breakrooms.
 
U.S. EXPORT CONTROL COMPLIANCE STATUS 
The person hired will have access to information and items subject to U.S. export controls, and therefore, must either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.62 or otherwise eligible for deemed export licensing. US persons include U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), and asylees and refugees with such status granted, not pending. 
 
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY
Hermeus is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions at Hermeus are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: Thermal Engineering Internship - Summer 2027
description:
About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
Spring internships will range between the months of January and May. All dates dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program.
As a part of the Thermal team you will get to work on the vehicle thermal analysis model to generate temperature predictions for our tests and missions. There may also be opportunities to run tests to verify our model predictions, create tools to help post-processing data, and design thermal hardware for the flight vehicle.
Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company’s success. You will be working on a collaborative team in a startup environment while being able to learn from some of most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the world. We’re dedicated to providing an experience that will let your decisions and contributions help drive Varda’s success.
Responsibilities
Support thermal vacuum (TVAC) test campaigns including setup, execution, and data collection
Contribute to thermal models for spacecraft components and systems using tools like Thermal Desktop and ANSYS
Analyze flight and ground test thermal data using Python and MATLAB
Design, procure, test, and validate thermal hardware (e.g., MLI blankets, heat straps, thermal interfaces)
Support integration and test (I&T) activities related to thermal components and subsystems
Collaborate with systems and mechanical teams to ensure thermal requirements are met
Basic Qualifications
Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or related Engineering discipline
Completed coursework in:
Heat Transfer
Thermodynamics
Fluid Mechanics
Data processing
Experience or coursework using thermal analysis software (e.g., Thermal Desktop, Ansys, Star CCM)
Proficiency in CAD tools (NX, AutoCAD, PTC, or similar)
Comfortable with data analysis in MATLAB and Python
Prior thermal internship, lab, project team, or rigorous school project experience relevant to heat transfer/thermal
Preferred Skills And Experience
Prior thermal internship experience in aerospace
Hardware procurement, build, and testing experience
Familiarity with spacecraft testing environments or aerospace systems
Experience working on a student design or competition team (e.g., rocketry, CubeSat, Formula SAE)
Leadership experience (demonstrated communication, organization, problem solving)
Compensation
Hourly Rate: $33.00
Housing stipend for interns relocating to the area
Commuter benefit to support local transportation
Benefits for Interns
Health & Wellness
Paid observed holidays
100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options
$120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses
Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents
Financial
$20/pay period cell phone reimbursement
Up to $4,000 gross up in relocation support, if eligible
Up to $850 commute credit through Lyft or car rental reimbursement, if eligible
Workplace Experience & Perks
Fully stocked kitchen with lunch provided daily and dinner provided twice weekly
Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and mission-success celebrations
Complimentary EV charging
ITAR Requirements
Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.
“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

title: Structures/Mechanical Engineering Intern - Spring/Summer 2027
description:

By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. About The Role: 
Hermeus is seeking a hands-on Structures/Mechanical Engineering Intern to support the design, build, and test of flight hardware for next-generation aircraft systems. In this role, you will help design and develop mechanical subassemblies across the vehicle, including control surfaces, landing gear doors, avionics trays, and other flight critical hardware.
This internship is ideal for students who enjoy owning real hardware, working in a fast-paced development environment, and taking designs from concept through fabrication, integration, and test.
Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April)
Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August)
Responsibilities
Support the design and development of flight hardware and mechanical subassemblies for aircraft systems.
Assist with CAD modeling, drawing creation, hardware release, and design updates.
Perform basic hand calculations and engineering analysis to support design decisions.
Help build, integrate, troubleshoot, and test prototype and flight hardware.
Collaborate with structures, mechanical, manufacturing, avionics, and test teams to support vehicle development.
Contribute to design reviews, test planning, and documentation of lessons learned.

description:

Familiarity with version control and collaborative development using Git or GitHub preferred
Enrollment at a college or university within a 250-mile radius of Omaha, Nebraska, required

title: Technical Program Manager Intern (Spring 2027)
description:
About Zipline
Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.
Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.
Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.
We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.
The Role
Zipline’s Program Management team is responsible for ensuring that Zipline achieves our company goals on time and on budget. Our PMs are embedded across our 6 hardware teams and work directly with engineers of many disciplines to design, build, and test our drones and ground infrastructure. Program managers define their team’s priorities and drive execution of key milestones in a constantly changing environment.
What You'll Do
Understand and mitigate technical and program risks to keep Zipline’s future programs on track. Drive decision making and trade off studies.
Define program timelines, milestones and critical path.
Manage and support cross-functional teams across electrical and mechanical engineering, design validation, and embedded software domains to build and execute a plan to develop new hardware
Drive prototype and test activities to validate next generation hardware designs
Report program updates to leadership
Manage new infrastructure builds for our test campaigns and track hardware sample allocations
Organize and facilitate meetings with cross-functional teams
Work closely with cross-functional groups to track incoming parts and quality
Manage upcoming hardware changes to meet company targets
What You'll Bring
Must have at least completed the second year of your undergraduate studies or equivalent in Mechanical or Mechatronics Engineering. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.
Strong technical background
Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain challenges and solutions to fellow engineers and non-engineers alike.
Enthusiasm for collaborating in a fast paced and highly cross-functional environment
Ability to pick up technical concepts rapidly
Ability to drive clarity amidst chaos and ambiguity
Extreme ownership and a bias for action
Must be eligible to work in the US
Demonstrated skill in aligning priorities, coordinating timelines, and leading complex scope, resource, and schedule trades
Must be able to work in person at Zipline’s South San Francisco office 5 days a week
What Else You Should Know
Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April/May.
The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.
Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.
Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.
We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!
Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

title: Platform Software Diagnostics Intern
description:
Platform Software Diagnostics Intern
Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site
About Astera Labs
Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions and software that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our platform software connects low-level device behavior, diagnostics, telemetry, validation, and fleet-scale manageability so customers can identify issues quickly and keep critical systems running.
The opportunity
Join the Platform Software Diagnostics team within Hardware Engineering and work at the boundary of software and hardware. You’ll help create practical tools for board and chip bring-up, production testing, validation, and data-driven debugging across Astera Labs’ product lines.
This internship is designed for someone who enjoys learning by doing: reading a specification, writing code, connecting to real hardware, running a test, investigating the result, and improving the tool or workflow. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to projects that turn low-level device behavior into reliable, understandable diagnostics.
What you’ll do
Develop and improve diagnostic utilities in C for board and chip bring-up, including register access, initialization, device discovery, and device-health checks.
Read schematics, specifications, register descriptions, and test output to understand expected hardware behavior and diagnose issues.
Write Python utilities and test automation to make validation, data collection, and debugging more repeatable.
Use Raspberry Pi-based lab systems and development tools to interact with boards, connectivity modules, and other hardware under test.
Create or maintain tests for production and validation workflows, helping identify failures earlier and improve test coverage.
Reproduce hardware/software issues, form hypotheses, run focused experiments, analyze evidence, and document findings.
Collaborate with engineers across diagnostics, validation, production, and related hardware/software teams to communicate results and deliver practical fixes.
Participate in code reviews, issue tracking, technical discussions, and documentation that make the team’s work easier to maintain and scale.
Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
Additional opportunities
Depending on project needs and your interests, you may also:
Investigate test results and failure logs, improving parsing, reporting, and data visualization so engineers can understand issues faster.
Contribute to regression and infrastructure projects, such as unit-test or pytest enablement, Jenkins workflows, time-series test data, or software-release automation.
What you bring
Hands-on experience with C, Python, or another programming language through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.
Curiosity about how software interacts with physical systems and a willingness to learn from schematics, specifications, registers, and test output.
Comfort working in a Linux development environment and using Git-based workflows.
A methodical approach to debugging: forming hypotheses, running focused tests, analyzing evidence, and documenting what you learn.
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to collaborate across software and hardware disciplines.
Ownership, persistence, and a practical mindset in an environment where the first attempt may not work.
Helpful experience
Embedded software, device drivers, bare-metal development, or low-level debugging.
I2C, SPI, PCIe, CXL, SerDes, signal-integrity concepts, or other hardware interfaces.
Raspberry Pi, lab automation, test equipment, or semiconductor/networking hardware.
Python test automation, pytest, log parsing, data analysis, or dashboard development.
Jenkins or other continuous-integration and regression systems.
Internship experience and compensation
This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour.
U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.
Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.
Equal opportunity
Astera Labs is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees. We value diverse perspectives and consider qualified candidates without regard to legally protected characteristics.
